Commentary.Commentary: 34 minutes to go for the break. Can New Zealand prize out a wicket or two? Stay tuned...
The KULCHA were at it again. 4 for Kuldeep, 2 for Chahal, with joint figures of 20-1-82-6. Shami was excellent with his three. No one was bad in particular.

India did the basics right, keeping the run flow tight. Shami got the ball to move around and the Kiwi openers were out in a jiffy. There was a bit of a stand between Taylor and Williamson but once the former was dismissed, the home side barely recovered. Kane Williamson fought hard but it was a lonely battle.

Guess Kuldeep has described it to perfection. On a batting wicket, where Simon Doull said that anything under 340 is not enough, the Kiwis are around 200 short. And none of the dismissals can be said due to the wicket. In fact, it has been skillful bowling.

Kuldeep says the ground size is small on one side. Mentions that him and Chahal just stick to the basics and get the success for it. Feels that it's a proper batting wicket and that 160-plus is chaseable. Reckons that these games are important for all three departments, keeping the upcoming World Cup in mind. Adds that there is support everywhere in the world for their side and it's amazing to see.
India will come out to bat for around 30 minutes. A poor batting performance from New Zealand on a good batting strip. Even Kuldeep Yadav says the same as here he is, giving an interview.

OUT! Edged to first slip. The innings is done. The googly outside off, Boult pushes at it, does not pick the line and gets a thick outside edge. Simple catch for Rohit Sharma. NEW ZEALAND GET BOWLED OUT FOR 157!
Dabs this behind point for a run.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
SIX! Not a bad shot. Full and around off, Southee gets down and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, the googly, Southee lunges to drive but is beaten.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
ALMOST CHOPS IT ON! Floated outside off, Boult goes back to push but drags it back on. It goes over the stumps.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
WIDE. Almost a stumping. Full and wide outside off, Boult comes down the track but then quickly drags his foot back in. Dhoni whips the bails off but Boult is safe. 150 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND.
Outside off, Trent goes across but then lets it go.
Well - if the Kiwis are bowled out before 0500 GMT, India will have to come out to bat till 0530 GMT.
Oh dear... jumps down the track, is nowhere near the pitch of the ball but then goes back to defend.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.

NOT OUT! Boult is lucky! Just has something behind behind the line. Trent doesn't read the wrong 'un and gets beaten. Dhoni takes the bails off and puts in another appeal. The umpire refers is up but Boult is lucky to have something behind the line.
Another stumping appeal. Is this the end of the innings?
Boult paddles this away towards fine leg and gets to the other end.
Gets behind the ball and bunts this one out.
Boult has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Trent Boult is the last man in.

OUT! MS Dhoni, enough said! Fligthed ball on off, spins away from Ferguson who comes ahead to push it to the off side. Gets beaten for the turn and Dhoni quickly does what he does best. Takes off the bails and then puts in an appeal. The umpire takes it up and replays show us that there is Ferguson has nothing behind the line. On the line is not good enough and Lockie has to walk. Ninth one down for the Kiwis.
Stumping appeal! Is Ferguson out of his crease?
Leg spin on off, driven to long off for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

DROPPED! That is a very casual effort. Shikhar Dhawan is the fielder. Full and around off, Southee looks to go inside out but finds Dhawan to perfection at wide long off. The fielder gets to his left, barely has to move but plonks it down. A single taken.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full again, watchfully blocked back.
Full and around off, pushed towards the bowler.

Huge, huge shout for LBW! Turned down! Kuldeep is on his haunches. Nearly had his third in this over. The googly again, around leg, Lockie had no idea about this as he looked to defend. Missed the line and was hit on the back pad. The umpire though, gave no thought to the appeal. Hawk Eye shows it to be dead plumb.
Lockie Ferguson comes in at number 10, replacing Bracewell.

OUT! Chopped on! Second wicket in the over and now, the Kiwis might not even see Powerplay 3. The googly outside off, short in length, Bracewell goes back to cut but does not pick the length or the line. Is too far from the ball and only gets a thick inside edge back onto the stumps.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Punches this off the back foot towards cover.
Full and around middle, almost pushed back to the bowler.
Tim Southee walks in at number 9, replacing his captain.

OUT! Caught in the deep! Williamson is gone and with that, the chances of a 250 or even a competitive score are gone too, one would think. First wicket for Kuldeep and he has got the trump card. The break has done the trick for the Indians. Beautifully tossed up around off, Williamson takes the gamble of going after the chinaman. The idea might have been wrong at this stage with not many wickets left. And it turns out to be a bad gamble. The skipper mistimes it and Vijay Shankar takes it comfortably at long on. Fabulous knock from the captain once again, under pressure. Upto his bowlers to make a match out of this.

DRINKS. India continue to do well on a track which does not seem to have too much for the bowlers. The wickets have fallen plainly due to consistent dogged bowling, not giving too much room. That sustained pressure has resulted in some shots being played out of frustration and eventually, wickets have fallen. 17 overs left and it does look a tall ask for the home side to bat out those. However, should Williamson stay till the end, 250 is a possibility. Whether that will be enough or not is a different question.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Stamping his authority. Full and around off, Bracewell gets one foot forward and lofts it with power over the bowler, almost dead-straight. One bounce and into the fence.
Pushes this through mid on for a run.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Around off, defended back to the bowler.
Goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Landed around off, watchfully blocked out.
Full once again, watchfully blocked out.
Around off, defended from the crease.
Around off again, pushed through the covers for a run.
Full and around off, Williamson paddles it gently through fine leg for a couple.
Kuldeep Yadav is back on. 6-0-26-0 so far.
On middle, pushed through mid on for a single.
Full and around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Around off, the googly, Williamson defends.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for a single.
Driven to the covers by the batsman. A successful over from Shami comes to an end.
A bouncer on middle, Bracewell ducks.
Doug Bracewell walks in at number 8, replacing Santner.

OUT! LBW! Plumb, plumb, dead plumb. When you get across, you cannot miss. If you miss, you get dismissed. That is exactly what has happened here. Santner walks across his stumps and Shami keeps it full and straight. Mitchell looks to flick but is beaten by pace. Is hit on the pads and is plumb in front. Shami appeals, the umpire takes his time but eventually raises his finger. Santner walks across slowly to Williamson to talk regarding the review and one reckons that if he had hit it, the review would have been taken straightaway. 'Can I, can I, should I?' probably are the questions asked by Santner. 'Nope. On your way son', might have been the response. A budding stand broken. Shami has his third.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, pushed past cover for a single.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Dot to end the over.  Santner has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Gets behind the ball and blocks this.

NOT OUT! Loopy ball outside off, Santner is drawn forward to play at it but misses it. Dhoni behind takes the bails off and appeals. Dhoni also thinks there is an edge so opts for the review. First they see the stumping but Santner makes it in time. Then they check caught behind but Snicko doesn't show any spike. So Santner survives and India lose their review.
Stumping appeal! Dhoni does not look too happy but let's see!
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Short ball, you get them with the leg spinner. Kane rocks back and pulls this through square leg and the ball crosses the ropes.
Leg spinner on the stumps, pushed to the cover region.
Changes his length by pitching it up in line of the stumps. Santner blocks it out.
FOUR! Not in total control but will take it. Short ball on the leg side, Santner looks to help it but gets a top edge which goes past Dhoni and into the fine leg boundary.
Pitches this one up further on the off side. Santner punches this to the off side.
Length again on the stumps, Santner blocks out another one.
Back of a length ball on the body. Santner gets his bat high and blocks this.
Length outside off, cut to deep point for one.
Mohammed Shami is back for another spell.
Covers his stumps and blocks this one in front of him. Good comeback from Kuldeep. 8 off the over.
Reads it again. This one is the straighter one. Outside off, Santner leaves it alone.
Comes into the southpaw who reads the spin and blocks it out.
Williamson gives room and creams this through covers for just one.
Goes back and punches this ball through cover-point for a single.
SIX! Not afraid to take the spinner on. Tossed up on middle, Santner gets under it and lofts this over long on. Maximum.
Covers his stumps and blocks this out to the off side.

Well done, Kane Williamson. Another half century to his name, his 36th in this format. The captain playing yet another vital knock for his side. Full and outside off, Williamson creams this through covers. Comes back for the second and gets to the milestone.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Slow and short outside off, Williamson cuts it towards covers and runs to the other end. Kuldeep collects and throws but fails to hit the target.
Slows this one on off, tapped to the off side and gets to the other end.
Outside off, driven to covers.
Short and outside off, punched towards the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Stays leg side of the ball and drives it towards long off for a run.
Full and around off, pushed back towards Kuldeep again.
Landed around off, the googly, pushed back to the bowler.
Tossed up outside off, pushed through mid off for a single.
Mitchell Santner is the new batsman in.

OUT! What a catch! Kuldeep Yadav has plucked one out from the air! Brilliant. Looped up ball on off, Nicholls looks to flick this but cannot keep this on the ground. Plays it uppishly towards mid on where Kuldeep dives to his weaker side, that is his right and sticks his arms out. The ball sticks and Nicholls has to walks back. The hosts have lost half their side and India's part-timer has a wicket.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
FOUR! Excellent placement. Knew where the fielder was and placed his sweep to perfection. Gets low and swipes this towards fine leg uppishly and the ball reaches the fence.
Punched off the back foot by Kane. No run taken.
On middle and leg, played to mid on and changes ends.
Outside off, punched off the back foot through cover-point. They pick up a single.
There is protection for that sweep shot. Williamson reaches for it and swipes this from outside off to fine leg. They cross to get the 100 on the board with the loss of 4 wickets.
Gets to the pitch of the ball and flicks this to mid-wicket.
Looped up again, Nicholls gets low and swipes it through mid-wicket for a single.
Gets behind this and turns his bat to the leg side. Dot ball.
Tossed up leg break on off, Williamson works it down on the leg side for a single.
Full and outside off, Henry reads it and leaves it alone.
Outside off, Kane cuts it towards backward point and rotates strike.
Outside off again, Nicholls punches it off his back foot to the off side. They take a run.
Pitched up outside off, driven to the man at covers.
Defended off the front foot by Nicholls presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Not the best start. Short and outside off, Nicholls stands inside and cuts it through point for a boundary. No fielder there and the balls runs away.
Kedar Jadav is into the attack. This is his 50th ODI match.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries for Kane. This is short outside off, Williamson rocks back and pulls it in the same region for another boundary. 10 runs from the over.
FOUR! What a shot! Lovely use of the feet and excellent placement. Comes down the track and clips this through mid-wicket. Bisects the field and the ball touches the ropes.
On the pads, flicked away with a wristy shot.
Nicholls has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Flighted ball on off, blocked towards mid on.
Tossed up on middle, turned to the leg side for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single.
Outside off, left alone. Williamson almost thought about playing that one but in the end, at the last moment, bailed out of the shot.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
The googly from Kuldeep, Nicholls misreads it, looks to defend but misses and is hit on the pads. The Indians appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Probably going down leg.
The batsman has driven it through mid off. They pick up a single.
Full on middle, pushed towards long on for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot. They pick up a single. 8 runs from the over but a wicket as well.
Henry Nicholls walks in at number 6, replacing Latham.

OUT! Oh dear me... do not stop the press. Would rather say, do not open the press today at all. Chahal has his second and guess what, both are caught and bowled. Another stinger. Full and around middle, Latham tries to do what he attempted on the previous ball, a chip down the ground. But this time, he hits it straight back to the bowler. Chahal lunges forward and takes it inches above the turf again (reference is to the Taylor wicket). He throws the ball up in the air and Latham initially throws his head skywards in disappointment and starts to walk. But then, stops. He expresses his feelings to the umpire regarding whether the ball has carried or not. The umpires have a customary chat and then refer it upstairs with the soft signal as OUT. There is nothing in the replays which can change the decision. Latham has to go and the strong Kiwi middle order is being broken.
Has Chahal got his second caught and bowled? He is claiming it but Latham ain't going anywhere. The umpires refer it upstairs with the soft signal as OUT.
FOUR! Lovely shot. Full and around middle, Latham comes forward and chips it beautifully over mid on. Shikhar Dhawan runs to his left from long on but the ball races away past him in a flash.
Pushes this past the bowler towards long on for a single.
Outside off, pushed to the off side.
On middle, Williamson goes back and helps it through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full and down the leg side, Latham gets down and paddles it fine for a couple.
Tossed up around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, punched down to long on for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Beaten first up! The googly outside off, Williamson looks to cut but is beaten.
KULCHA TIME. Officially. Kuldeep Yadav into the attack.
Goes back and works it through the leg side for a couple.
Outside off, punched off the back foot for one.
Down the leg side, flicked through the leg side for a run.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

DROPPED! Oh dear! Kedar Jadav has put down the Kiwi skipper. Short ball on the hips, Williamson pulls it away but finds Kedar at deep square leg. Jadav gets low but cannot hold onto it. Big miss this, how costly will it prove?
Full and on off, Williamson on-drives it to mid on.
Kane has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On the leg side again, Williamson tucks it away to deep square leg and they come back for the second.
FOUR! Nicely done and well in control. Not too short, Kane checks his pull and just glances this away through square leg. The fine leg fielder is fine and the ball touches the ropes.
On off, Williamson defends it off his back foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and down the leg side, swept fine for a single.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Tom Latham walks in at number 5, replacing Taylor.

OUT! CAUGHT AND BOWLED! Boy. Stop the press. Chahal has taken a caught and bowled dismissal. That too, with the ball dipping onto him. Beautifully flighted outside off, Taylor comes forward to push but cannot keep it down. The ball dips onto the bowler who does well to take it inches above the ground. Fabulous catch. Usually, Chahal struggles to take such stuff but not today.
A bit of extra flight, Taylor stays leg side of the ball, reaches out to drive but mistimes it back to Chahal.
Tossed up around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
FOUR! Classic shot. On a length outside off, Williamson gets on top of the bounce and punches it through the covers. No soul can stop it. 50 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover where Rayudu fumbles and concedes a single.

FOUR! That is a superb shot. Simply superb. Tell you why. The ball is short and Taylor unfurls the cut shot. What is so superb about that, you ask? Alright. Let me give you some talking points first. Twice or thrice in a row, Rosco was connecting the cut shot but straight to the fielder. So now, he adjusts. Cuts the ball hard, into the ground close to him so powerfully that it bounces over the leaping point fielder and races to the fence. Small adjustments sometimes provide fruitful results.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a run.
Goes back and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Short in length, cut through the covers for a single.
Floated outside off, pushed towards cover.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.
Time for breakfast? Or lunch? The 'CHA' of KULCHA is about to be served. Yuzvendra Chahal into the attack.
On middle and leg, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Pushes this towards mid on, takes on Ambati Rayudu who is pretty lazy and completes the single with ease.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short and outside off, a cracking cut shot but straight to point.
On middle and leg, helped through square leg for a single.

SAFE! Taylor is well in. Many batsmen get out these days in such fashion. Full and around off, Williamson gets forward and across and drives it straight back. Shankar looks to stop it with a bend in his follow through and the ball deflects off his hands behind. Hits the stumps and India appeal confidently. It is referred upstairs but replays show that Rosco stretched well enough to get back in before the ball hit the stumps.
Is that a run out? Will be a freakish way to get out if Rosco is gone...
Tossed up outside off, Williamson drives it to long off to retain strike for the next over.
Outside off, Taylor rocks back and cuts it to deep point for another run.
Loopy ball on the pads, tucked away around the corner for nothing.
On middle and leg, played with a straight bat to mid on. They cross.
Leg spinner on the same line, this time Ross gets it to deep point and rotates ends.
Leg spinner on off. Gets turn on that one. Taylor gets a bottom edge trying to cut it.
Yuzvendra Chahal to roll his arm now.
Full on off, Williamson punches it back to the bowler. Good start for Shankar.
Slightly outside off, Kane tries to run it down but cannot get it past the short third man fielder.
Full and on that off stump again. Williamson who is not getting much of the strike recently is happy to block it.
Outside off, guided down to third man to change ends.
Length ball on that off stump, Taylor offers a defensive stroke.
Angles this full on the pads, Taylor gives it to short mid-wicket. Dhawan dives and stops the runs.
Vijay Shankar is the first change.
Good stop. Fuller than the previous ball around off. Taylor gently pushes it towards mid off. Good stop from the fielder but the batsmen manage to cross.
Slightly fuller than that good length. Taylor pushes it to cover-point.
On top of off, Taylor taps it to the off side.
FOUR! Cutting loose is Taylor! Pitched up ball on off, Ross shimmies down a bit and lofts this through the line over mid-wicket for a one-bounce boundary.
Similar line teasing Ross who is happy to block it out.
Length on that fourth stump channel, blocked by Taylor.
KW plays it with an angled bat and guides it to short third man.

Chance but a fumble! On off, Taylor with soft hands pushes it towards mid-wicket and hares to complete the run. Rayudu there looks to collect it with his weaker arm but fails to do so. Would have been tight had he hit.
FOUR! Magnificent shot! Taylor is in good form and it's showing. Short ball outside off, Taylor quickly gets into position and pulls it through mid-wicket. The ball races away to the fence.
Back of a length around off, Taylor shuffles across and flicks it away through square leg for a brace.
Lovely! In line of the stumps on a good length. Taylor get behind it and sees it out.
Corrects his length by giving it on off and full. Taylor pushes it to the cover-point region.
WIDE! Shami tries surprising Taylor with a bouncer but bangs it way too short. Wide given by the umpire.
Very tidy over. Just one form it. On off, Williamson defends it from within his crease.
Still cannot find the gap. Back of a length outside off, Williamson hops and punches it. Yet again to the fielder at cover-point.
On off, driven to point for nothing.
Full and around off, Taylor gives it towards mid on and gets to the other end. Very important for the Kiwis to rotate the strike.
Full and a bit outside off. First opportunity of width. Taylor looks to cut it but cannot get it past Kohli at point.
No room to pay with. Taylor bunts it in front of him.
A maiden. Second for Shami. Brilliant stuff. Pitches it in line, Williamson blocks it out.
Test him with a bounce now. Williamson ducks to evade it. 5 dot balls.

JUST SHORT! That would have been a third for Shami. Pitches it up and changes his length. Serves this wider and invites Williamson for the drive. Kane reaches for it and uppishly drives it to Kohli at point. The Indian skipper dives forward but it falls just short of him.
Angles this from over the wicket into Williamson who defends it with a straight bat.
Similar line and length, this time Kane taps it to backward point.
Length closer to the stumps. Williamson gets a bottom edge which goes past the stumps.
In line of the stumps, Taylor turns his bat to the on side. Just one run from the over. Terrific from Bhuvi. Finding his line after being slightly wayward in his first.
Serves this full now on off, RT on-drives it to mid on for nothing.
Peach! Length on a good length. Moves away after pitching. Ross feels for it and almost gets his outside edge. India are right on the money.
Fuller this time outside off, Rosco is happy to defend it.
On that good length again targeting the off stump. Taylor pushes it back towards the bowler.
Around off, Williamson runs it down to third man to give Ross the strike.
Length outside off, Taylor punches it but gives it to the man at cover-point. Excellent from Shami after being hit for a lovely boundary first up. 5 runs and a wicket from it.
Pitches it up further around off. Taylor gets behind it and blocks it well.
A bit short outside off, Taylor watches it go through to the keeper.
Ross Taylor walks in next, at number 4, replacing Munro.

OUT! Shami you beauty! Second wicket in two overs and he is roaring. On a good length, gets the ball nipping back into the left-hander. Munro looks to drive it but is totally beaten. The ball goes on to hit the top of middle and New Zealand lose their second wicket. Excellent line and length from Shami. New Zealand's openers are back in the hut. Another dangerous batsman dismissed.
Back of a length around off, comes back into Williamson who tucks it away on the on side.
FOUR! CLASS! Kane Williamson special! Slightly overpitched outside off, Williamson gets forward and just punches this through covers. From the sweet spot and away she goes.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! That is Munro's area. Full and outside off, Munro goes over mid off and clears the fielder comfortably. Almost clears the ropes.

FOUR! That is a terrific shot! The timing is excellent. The length is not all that bad, fractionally short of a good length but Munro just lifts his right leg up and plays a Nataraja pull shot through mid-wicket!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Around middle, watchfully defended.
On off, Williamson defends this from within the crease.
Kane Williamson is in at no. 3.

OUT! Shami strikes! Becomes the fastest to 100 ODI wickets for India. Sets up Guptill perfectly. Inswing, outswing and now another ball moving away. On a good length around off. Moves away a tad. Martin looks to play it on the off side but gets a faint edge and onto the stumps. The lights flash and India are up in celebration. Martin Guptill is a huge wicket. Shami goes past Irfan Pathan to become the fastest Indian to 100 ODI wickets, who took it in 59 games. This is Shami's 56th ODI.
Outside off, swinging away Guptill leaves it alone.

Long appeal this time and a confident one but the umpire stays put. Inswinging length ball on off, comes back in. Guptill offers no shot and gets rapped on the pads. India don't opt for a review. Looks like height was the only issue there.
Similar length on middle and off. Martin strides forward to block it but gets an inside edge onto his pads. Shami appeals but it dies down.
On a good length, on middle and leg. Guptill tucks it away on the on side.
Mohammad Shami to bowl from the other end. He is just one away from 100 ODI wickets.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. Exclude that boundary ball and it is a wonderful start from Bhuvi.
On middle and leg, watchfully patted back to the bowler.
Down the leg side again, flicked away once more but this time fine leg has been placed much squarer. He is moved to long leg and hence, it is just a single.
Outside off, gentle outswing, left alone.

FOUR! Wonderful timing. Bhuvi drifts on the pads and the length is a bit too full. Guptill flicks it uppishly but wide of the fielder at short mid-wicket. In fact, it is through square leg and the ball races away. Fine leg has no chance. First runs of the match.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

The anthems are done and we are ready for the game to begin. Let us have a stat to start. This is India's 1600TH INTERNATIONAL GAME - third most after Australia (1854) and England (1833). Out come the players. Martin Guptill and Colin Munro are the openers for New Zealand. Bhuvneshwar Kumar to start off with the first new ball. Guppy to face. Here we go...
Time for the national anthems. India's first up...

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull says that Napier has not hosted an international game for more than 2 years. Feels that the grass has been rolled nicely and we should have plenty of runs. Expects at least 340 for the side batting first to win.

Indian captain, Virat Kohli, says that Indian bowlers have played a bigger role than the batsmen in the last 12-18 months but do not get enough credit because it has become a batsman's game. People want to see more of fours and sixes, he adds. Stresses that his side is very balanced, confident and relaxed, knowing its abilities well. Is expecting a rough contest, that too in the right spirit. Adds that there is mutual respect between the two sides, so here will be competition along with fun. On motivation, Kohli says that his team needs no such motivation to play for the country. On the aggression comparison with the Kiwis, Virat opines that the body language of the Black Caps may not be the same as that of the Aussies but their passion to win shows their aggression.

New Zealand skipper, Kane Williamson, says that it looks a very good surface and usually stays the same throughout. Admits that India are usually a very good chasing side but he wants to focus on his own side's strength. Informs that they are going in with one spinner with Mitchell Santner making a comeback. Adds further that the team combination is more due to balance. Wants to keep improving in all aspects but particularly stresses on the fielding part, which was not the best against the Lankans.
TOSS time. The necessary people are out in the middle. Heads is the call from Kohli but it is a Tail. NEW ZEALAND OPT TO BAT FIRST.

WEATHER - First up in New Zealand, one looks at the skies. Sunil Gavaskar laments, India's luck in this country has been such that they always get cloudy skies and green tracks. However, today, Sunny is smiling because it is nice and sunny. Not a cloud in the sky.

Having not won a series here in a decade India will look to change that record. They now have their own 10-year challenge. Kohli vs Kane is going to be Fire vs Ice. It's almost set-up for the top order to decide the games for both teams. New Zealand have a pacy attack and that will surely test the shaky Indian middle order. For the hosts, their main examination will be to see out the Indian spinners. It will be interesting to see what combinations do the teams go for. Toss and team news not far away.
